BIBLIOGRAPHIC RECORD

William Penn. (1644–1718).  Fruits of Solitude.
The Harvard Classics.  1909–14.

Part I

Detraction

267. Have a care of that base Evil Detraction. It is the Fruit of Envy, as that is of Pride; the immediate Offspring of the Devil: Who, of an Angel, a Lucifer, a Son of the Morning, made himself 
a Serpent, a Devil, a Beelzebub, and all that is obnoxious to the Eternal Goodness.
268. Vertue is not secure against Envy. Men will Lessen what they won’t Imitate.
269. Dislike what deserves it, but never Hate: For that is of the Nature of Malice; which is almost ever to Persons, not Things, and is one of the blackest Qualities Sin begets in the Soul.
